newsitem.title: USA: Firm settles with CFTC, SEC over derivatives trades.
newsitem.headline: Firm settles with CFTC, SEC over derivatives trades.

text.p: First Capital Strategists will pay $2.6 million and leave the securities and futures industries to settle charges the firm and its four partners failed to supervise trades which caused one of its biggest customers to lose $137.6 million, regulators said Wednesday.

Without admitting or denying any wrong-doing, the York, Pa, investment firm and its principals settled separate administrative proceedings of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The $2.6 million in restitution will be turned over to the client, Common Fund, a manager of endowments for 1,400 colleges and universities, which lost millions as the result of unauthorized trades made between 1992 and June 1995 by former derivatives trader Kent Ahrens, an SEC official said.
"This case is important because it's not just a failure to supervise," said Cheryl Scarboro, the SEC attorney handling the case. There was a "complete absence" of supervision, she said.

"Mr. Ahrens for many years was a very instrumental and profitable aspect for the firm. He was given a lot of leeway and supervisors had a lot of faith in him and that's just not enough in the SEC's view," Scarboro said.

Ahrens last year settled federal charges and pled guilty to related criminal charges. For years, Ahrens bet with Common Fund money, without hedging, that the stock market would decline, regulators said. As the market continued rising, losses in the Common Fund account mounted, regulators said, and Ahrens allegedly concealed those losses.

"The partners informed the Common Fund immediately when they discovered the losses," said Joe Goldstein, an attorney with Crowell & Moring, who is representing the firm. "Everyone involved regrets the losses the Common Fund suffered," he said.
